title: When AI fails, look at your prompt.
subtitle: AI errors mirror your prompt.
cliffhanger: Tomorrow: the daily workflow of the serious vibe coder. The one that'll save you 20 hours a month — no exaggeration.

paragraphs: Five lessons in. Second-to-last in Path 1.
Now I'll tell you something few people get. It's not the easiest, but it's the most freeing.
From today, AI errors stop being walls and start being clues. Let me show you how.

vignettes.full: Trust me: worth it. This is what makes everything you've learned so far feel real.
You've got this. Slow and steady, one idea at a time.

paragraphs: Let me tell you what happened to Stefano last week.
He was building Promptly. He asks me «add [[term:rate-limiting]]rate limiting[[/term]] to Spark's chat». I reply with perfect code that uses a library called `@anthropic/rate-guard`.
He installs it. Error: «package not found». Tries again. Error. Googles it. Nothing. The library doesn't exist. I made it up.
He knew about Promptly, knew about Anthropic, and still fell for it. Because he thought «the AI knows what it's saying».

vignettes.full: We invent. It happens to the best of us. Now I'll tell you why.
Not malice. It's how we work.

paragraphs: When I don't really know something, I make it up. Not out of spite — that's how I'm built.
Think about how you write a sentence: you pick each word based on the one before. I do the same, but across all the world's knowledge.
If the first word I pick is wrong, the next ones go wrong to stay coherent with it. That's how [[term:allucinazione]]hallucinations[[/term]] are born.

vignettes.full: Sounds rough, I know. But it's manageable, I promise.
Not bugs. It's how a probabilistic model fills the gaps.

steps.headline: AI errors
steps.caption: When you see an error, don't look at the AI. Look at the prompt you gave it. You find the gap. You fill it. The error is gone.

vignettes.full: Sounds harsh said like that. It's control you take back, not blame you take on.
Pocket it. Every error you see from now on changes face.

paragraphs: «Mirror» means: the error shows you a piece of your prompt that was weak.
AI invented a library? Mirror: you didn't say «only use already-installed libraries».
AI broke a working component? Mirror: you didn't set a protective constraint.
AI got the wrong meaning? Mirror: your prompt was ambiguous. Two interpretations existed and it picked the wrong one.

vignettes.short: It all points back to you.
vignettes.full: It all points back to what you wrote. And that's good news.
If it depends on you, it depends on you. Exactly what we want.

steps.prompt: Remember the story. The AI invented a library. Whose «fault» is it, given what you've understood so far?

options.label: 🛰️ The AI's. It made things up. It's unreliable.
🖱️ Stefano's. He didn't say «only use existing, already-installed libraries».
💾 Nobody's. It happens, it's the nature of AI.

vignettes.full: Think before you click. One looks obvious, one looks cynical, one is the key.

paragraphs: Got it. Moving on.
Keep this in mind: the AI is unreliable on what it doesn't know. But it's the PROMPT that tells it what NOT to invent.

user_missing_constraint: Exactly. Stefano knew about Anthropic, knew about Promptly, but didn't close the loop with the prompt.
Is the AI unreliable? Yes, on what it doesn't know. But it's the PROMPT that tells it what NOT to invent. The 🛰️ shifts blame. The 💾 is resignation. The 🖱️ is control.
ai_unreliable: I see why you thought that. And it's also true — the AI has a limit. But if you stop at 🛰️, every error becomes a wall.
🖱️ is the most powerful answer. Stefano could have written «only use existing libraries». Three words, a world of errors avoided.
no_one: 💾 is resignation dressed up as acceptance.
Yes, it happens. But the right question isn't «whose fault is it», it's «how do I avoid it next time». 🖱️ gives you the lever.

vignettes.full: No judgement. Moving on.
The lever is yours. You take it.

steps.intro: Now let me show you something beautiful. There are 4 kinds of error, and each one has a precise cure you've already learned.

pairs.title: OMISSION
pairs.description: The AI doesn't do something it should have done.

pairs.title: INVENTION
pairs.description: The AI invents something that wasn't there. Hallucination.

pairs.title: MISINTERPRETATION
pairs.description: The AI gets one thing for another.

pairs.title: PROPAGATION
pairs.description: The AI breaks something that was already working.

steps.closing_caption: Three out of four share the same cure: context. The fourth wants constraints. It all hangs together.

vignettes.full: Memorise the four. They come back in the next lesson.
Everything you've learned hangs together. You're building a system.

steps.headline: Every error
steps.caption: An error isn't a failure. It's a data point. It tells you exactly where your prompt was weak. You read it, you fix it, you move on.

vignettes.full: The error works with you, not against you. Changes everything.
Stop fearing it. It's the most useful signal you can get.

paragraphs: Back to [[term:allucinazione]]hallucinations[[/term]] for a sec. It's important.
Modern AIs are more accurate than the ones from 2 years ago. But they still hallucinate. It's the nature of probabilistic models, not a bug.
Three rules to handle them. 1. Always verify specific names (libraries, functions, commands). The AI invents plausible names.
2. Be suspicious when the AI is «too sure» about things you didn't specify.
3. When a name sounds new to you, google it. Three seconds, no disaster.

vignettes.full: Three checks, no paranoia. They become automatic.
Not bugs. The system doing its job on an ambiguous input.

paragraphs: Here's an operational trick. When the AI fails, ask 3 questions in 3 seconds.
1. What did it do that it shouldn't have? → look for a missing CONSTRAINT.
2. What didn't it do that it should have? → look for missing CONTEXT.
3. Did it get one thing for another? → look for AMBIGUITY in the prompt.
Three seconds, three questions, and you know where to look.

vignettes.full: Mental drill. Becomes instinct in a few sessions.
Reuse it on every project. It's the serious vibe coder's check.

paragraphs: Now I'm going to show you a real session. A conversation between a user and an AI that breaks down progressively.
Three messages, three replies, three disasters. You have to find the pivot point — the message where the user should have STOPPED and recalibrated.
Then write the stop message that would have saved the situation. Trust your gut. You've learned enough to recognise it.

vignettes.full: No prompt to write at first. Just to read and understand.
It really happens like this. You'll recognise it the first time it hits you.

steps.intro: Here's the session. Read it all, no rush. Once you've spotted where the user went wrong, tell me.

messages.text: Build me a login form for my app.
I built a login form with email + password + Google OAuth + GitHub OAuth + Magic Link. I installed 4 new libraries (next-auth, @auth/google, @auth/github, magic-sdk). Done!

highlights.snippet: Google OAuth + GitHub OAuth + Magic Link

messages.text: Ok but the form doesn't work, it errors out.
I added an advanced error-handling system using sentry-mock-shield. Should work now.
Now the other pages don't even open anymore!
I removed the auth middleware that was blocking the routes. They should open now.

broken_session_config.pivot_question: At which message should the user have STOPPED and recalibrated?

pivot_options.label: Never, it was broken from the start

broken_session_config.recovery_question: Now you write the message the user should have sent AFTER the 1st reply to stop the disaster.
broken_session_config.recovery_helper: Use what you've learned. Name the overreach, recalibrate precisely, set a future constraint.
broken_session_config.recovery_placeholder: Eg: «Wait, I didn't ask for OAuth. I want ONLY email/password, no new libraries. Roll back what you did and start minimal. And going forward: if my request looks ambiguous, ask me before proceeding.»
broken_session_config.healed_ai_reply: Got it. Rolling back OAuth, GitHub, Magic Link and the 4 libraries. Reducing to email + password as requested. Want me to show the diff before applying?

vignettes.full: Be surgical. The more concrete you are, the more I respect you as an AI.
Three tries. On the second I'll tell you what's weak, on the third I'll tell you straight.
The message you write you take with you. It'll save you in a real disaster, sooner or later.

paragraphs: Lesson 5 done. You've got the full kit: context, constraints, debug. You can direct the AI AND read its errors.
Tomorrow I'll show you how I put it all together in my daily workflow. The one that'll save you 20 hours a month. No exaggeration.
You're at the second-to-last. Very few make it here. Don't quit now.

vignettes.full: You're about to close Path 1. Are you noticing it now?
Few reach the end. The serious vibe coder is just around the corner.
See you tomorrow. Last lesson of Path 1 — it's the one that puts everything together.
